source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of EEG Foundation Models via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: W. Lehn-Schiøler; Magnus Ruud Kjær; Rahul Thapa; Magnus Guldberg Pedersen; A. Storgaard; N. Williams; Radu Gatej; T. Lehn-Schiøler; A. Brink-Kjær; S. Puthusserypady; S. Beniczky; James Zou; Lars Kai Hansen

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present. Figures are referenced but their graphical contents are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses sparse autoencoders to interpret EEG foundation models, motivated in part by superposition, and reports how its own SAE-based attribution and steering framework performs. It does not measure individual-neuron polysemanticity or test the claim versions as stated.
record.gate_note: The paper measures semanticity and entanglement of SAE dictionary features, not individual neurons. The text reports two qualitative steering examples in which concepts degrade together through entanglement; these concern SAE features and clinical concepts, so they are recorded under fits_no_version rather than linked to a neuron-focused version. Numerical taxonomy fractions shown in Figures 3–5 cannot be extracted from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study cites superposition as the reason neurons are uninterpretable and uses TopK SAEs as a tool on EEG transformers. It reports SAE-feature taxonomy fractions, concept encoding and steering selectivity. It never measures how often or how strongly individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs. Its 'Entangled (polysemantic co-activations)' class applies to SAE dictionary features tied to clinical concepts, not to model neurons. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors present a model-agnostic SAE, concept-steering and spectral-decoding framework that maps where clinical concepts are selectively steerable, entangled or weakly encoded. They expose 'wrecking-ball' interventions and age–pathology entanglement, and pitch the framework as a diagnostic tool for clinical trust. They also stress that SAE reconstruction preserves classification AUROC within 0.017.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains layer-wise TopK sparse autoencoders, attributes SAE features to predefined clinical concepts, and steers feature activations; it does not use the original neuron-focused method. It also uses EEG foundation models rather than the original source settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports variation across encoder, layer, and SAE expansion factor; it also describes selectivity as differing by target concept and layer. The supplied text does not give extractable numerical taxonomy fractions for those settings.

fits_no_version.finding: In some encoder, layer and concept settings, clamping concept-aligned SAE features degrades target and off-target clinical concepts in lockstep (excess selectivity ≈ 0). Examples are SleepFM L1 psychiatric medication and LaBraM L4 age, both against abnormality, plus abnormality in REVE layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clinical concepts in EEG foundation-model SAE features are often entangled, so one cannot be suppressed without degrading another.

fits_no_version.finding: The share of entangled versus separable SAE features varies with encoder, layer and SAE expansion factor (Figure 3). Numbers are not readable from the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature monosemanticity in EEG transformers depends on layer depth and dictionary expansion.

record.problems: The paper's concept taxonomy is investigator-defined and limited to available cohort metadata. Its reported entanglement examples are qualitative in the supplied text, and the numerical taxonomy and steering results are presented in figures whose graphical contents are absent here. The study concerns SAE features rather than individual neurons.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-based taxonomy fractions and steering-curve values in Figures 3–5 were not extracted because the supplied text contains captions but not the plotted values. No additional text-only result directly measures the neuron-focused claim versions.

untested.parts: No image classifiers and no neuron-level analysis.
No language-model MLP neurons are examined. The EEG transformers' neurons are never characterized directly.
Superposition is assumed as motivation, not tested.
Separable, entangled and dead fractions vary across encoders and layers, but only for SAE features. There is no neuron share and no activation-function or regularization manipulation.
Not addressed for neurons. The SAE taxonomy depends on the expansion factor, but that concerns SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: T4 is appropriate. The paper uses superposition and SAEs as tools and reports its own pipeline's performance. Its use of 'polysemantic' refers to SAE features co-activating with several clinical concepts, not to neurons. The figure-based taxonomy values are absent from the text, but they would not bear on any version anyway.

versions.untested_parts: Individual neurons in image classifiers and the stated image-input examples.
MLP neurons in language models and polysemanticity across transformer layers.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than there are neurons.
Polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when there is sufficient neuron capacity.
The share of polysemantic neurons, its change with activation function or regularization, and any associated performance cost. The study compares SAE feature representations, not neurons.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons detect one shared feature or related offshoots, and whether truly unrelated neuron mixtures are rare.
Whether polysemanticity depends on the examined activation range or on how explanations are scored.

rows.subject: SleepFM
rows.stage_stated: Finetuned end-to-end on the binary normal/abnormal target
rows.operation_detail: Clamped TCAV-aligned SAE features toward a target centroid and evaluated target and off-target probes.
rows.measure: Target and off-target probe AUROC degradation under steering; the paper describes both concepts as degrading through entanglement.
rows.value: Both concepts degrade through entanglement; numeric AUROCs not stated in the text.
rows.note: This is a qualitative SAE-feature steering result, not a measurement of individual-neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: This row records target and off-target entanglement of SAE features under steering in SleepFM L1 (psychiatric medication vs abnormality). It does not measure neuron polysemanticity, and it gives no numeric AUROC. The state relative to any version cannot be determined, though the record's 'observed' is fine for the finding itself.
